Paper_Title: Comparative analysis of text-based plagiarism detection techniques
Authors: M. Sajid, M. Sanaullah, M. Fuzail, T. S. Malik, S. M. Shuhidan
Original_Problem: Systematic benchmarking of computational efficiency and lexical versus semantic trade-offs in academic plagiarism detection
Implemented_Algorithm: Sublinear TF-IDF vectorization with pairwise cosine similarity metric and validation threshold tuning
Dataset_Compatibility: Fully compatible with MIT/SNLI text pairs
Adaptation_Details: Implemented as lightweight lexical baseline and Tier-1 text pre-filter

Paper_Title: A comprehensive strategy for identifying plagiarism in academic submissions
Authors: D. M. Setu, T. Islam, M. Erfan, S. K. Dey, M. R. Al Asif, M. G. R. Alam
Venue: Journal of Umm Al-Qura University for Engineering and Architecture (Springer)
Original_Problem: Detection of verbatim and paraphrased academic text plagiarism across digital submissions
Implemented_Algorithm: Sentence-BERT (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) 384-dimensional contextual sequence embeddings with mean pooling and cosine distance metric
Dataset_Compatibility: Evaluated on MIT plagiarism dataset in original paper
Adaptation_Details: Implemented faithfully using offline-cached Hugging Face transformers/sentence-transformers as heavy semantic detector

Paper_Title: A Support Vector Machine based approach for plagiarism detection in Python code submissions in undergraduate settings
Authors: N. Gandhi, K. Gopalan, P. Prasad
Original_Problem: Overcoming token-based limitations (MOSS/JPlag) under student code obfuscations in undergraduate assignments
Implemented_Algorithm: Multi-dimensional feature engineering (comment stripping, token Jaccard, anonymized identifier matching, keyword distribution cosine, operator overlap, cyclomatic complexity proxy, line count ratio) fitted to an RBF Support Vector Machine
Dataset_Compatibility: Evaluated on undergraduate programming assignments; adapted to IR-Plag Java Corpus
Adaptation_Details: Faithfully adapted from Python AST to Java lexical and syntactic structures; tested across Faidhi-Robinson levels L1-L6

Paper_Title: Typed-Decision Pre-Filtering for Cost-Efficient Academic Integrity Detection Pipelines
Original_Problem: Quadratic computational scaling penalty and recall collapse in multi-modal academic integrity pipelines
Implemented_Algorithm: Modality-aware typed routing + validation-calibrated tri-band confidence filtering (Low Risk [Pruned], Uncertain [Escalated], High Risk [Flagged])
Dataset_Compatibility: Evaluated across MIT/SNLI text benchmark and IR-Plag Java corpus
Adaptation_Details: Novel architecture integrating M1/M2/M3 into an adaptive, recall-preserving triage pipeline
